questions.q: Where did Yahweh tell Moses to send some men?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to send some men to examine the land of Canaan, which he had given to the people of Israel.

questions.q: What was the rank of the men who were sent from among the people of Israel?
questions.a: All of the men were leaders from every tribe among the people of Israel.

questions.q: What name did Moses use for Hoshea son of Nun who was chosen?
questions.a: Moses called Hoshea son of Nun by the name of Joshua.

questions.q: What did Moses tell the men to observe about the people who lived in the land?
questions.a: Moses told the men to observe the people who lived there, whether they were strong or weak, few or many.

questions.q: What did Moses tell the men to notice about the cities in the land?
questions.a: Moses told them to see if the cities were like camps or fortified cities.

questions.q: What did Moses tell the leaders to find out about the land and what were they to bring back?
questions.a: Moses told the leaders to see whether the land was good for growing crops, whether there were trees, and to bring back samples of produce.

questions.q: What did the men cut down in the Valley of Eschol?
questions.a: When the men reached the Valley of Eshcol, they cut down a branch with a cluster of grapes.

questions.q: How many men did it take to bring back the cluster of grapes, and what else did the people bring back?
questions.a: It took two men to carry the grapes on a staff; their group also brought pomegranates and figs.

questions.q: How long did the men spend examining the land?
questions.a: The men returned from examining the land after forty days.

questions.q: To whom did they bring back word besides Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: They also brought back word to all the community of the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did the men report about the people in the land?
questions.a: The men reported that the people who made their homes in the land were strong.

questions.q: What word did the men return about the cities in the land?
questions.a: The men returned word that the cities were fortified and very large.

questions.q: When did Caleb encourage the people to attack the land?
questions.a: Caleb encouraged the people to attack it at once.

questions.q: Why did the other men who had gone with Caleb say they were not able to attack the people?
questions.a: The other men who had gone with Caleb said they were not able to attack the people because they were stronger than they were.

questions.q: How did the men describe how small they felt compared to the giants of the land?
questions.a: The men said that in their own sight they were like grasshoppers in comparison with the giants of the land.

commentary.text: Twelve men sent to search the land of Canaan, Their instructions.

Verses 1–20 A memorable and melancholy history is related in this and the following chapter, of the turning back of Israel from the borders of Canaan, and the sentencing them to wander and perish in the wilderness, for their unbelief and murmuring. It appears, De 1:22, that the motion to search out the land came from the people. They had a better opinion of their own policy than of God's wisdom. Thus we ruin ourselves by believing the reports and representations of sense rather than Divine revelation. We walk by sight not by faith. Moses gave the spies this charge, Be of good courage. It was not only a great undertaking they were put upon, which required good management and resolution; but a great trust was reposed in them, which required that they should be faithful. Courage in such circumstances can only spring from strong faith, which Caleb and Joshua alone possessed.

The searchers of the land brought a bunch of grapes with them, and other fruits, as proofs of the goodness of the country; which was to Israel both the earnest and the specimen of all the fruits of Canaan. Such are the present comforts we have in communion with God, foretastes of the fulness of joy we expect in the heavenly Canaan. We may see by them what heaven is.

We may wonder that the people of Israel staid forty days for the return of their spies, when they were ready to enter Canaan, under all the assurances of success they could have from the Divine power, and the miracles that had hitherto attended them. But they distrusted God's power and promise. How much we stand in our own light by our unbelief! At length the messengers returned; but the greater part discouraged the people from going forward to Canaan. Justly are the Israelites left to this temptation, for putting confidence in the judgment of men, when they had the word of God to trust in. Though they had found the land as good as God had said, yet they would not believe it to be as sure as he had said, but despaired of having it, though Eternal Truth had engaged it to them. This was the representation of the evil spies. Caleb, however, encouraged them to go forward, though seconded by Joshua only. He does not say, Let us go up and conquer it; but, Let us go and possess it. Difficulties that are in the way of salvation, dwindle and vanish before a lively, active faith in the power and promise of God. All things are possible, if they are promised, to him that believes; but carnal sense and carnal professors are not to be trusted. Unbelief overlooks the promises and power of God, magnifies every danger and difficulty, and fills the heart with discouragement. May the Lord help us to believe! we shall then find all things possible.
